name: York
note: Town of York founded 1793 by Simcoe; incorporated as the City of Toronto on 6 March 1834.

name: Toronto
note: York renamed and incorporated as the City of Toronto, 6 March 1834.

name: The Garrison
note: Garrison established by Simcoe in 1793; first called the Garrison / the Garrison at York. Called the Old Fort after new fortifications were built in 1841. to_year 1870 = start of the decade in which the source says 'Fort York' came into use (1870s, no exact year).

name: Fort York
note: Name is a retronym; source says usage emerged 'during the 1870s' (no exact year, 1870 used). Original fort destroyed 1813, rebuilt 1813-1815.

name: The Peninsula
note: The islands were a peninsula ('the long beach or peninsula') until a storm on 13 April 1858 cut a permanent channel; first breached 1852 but refilled.

name: Toronto Islands
note: Peninsula became an island permanently on 13 April 1858; City acquired the Islands in 1867.

name: Toronto Harbour
note: Source: 'Toronto Harbour or Toronto Bay'. Both names are used; no date given for either. from_year = map start.

name: Lake Ontario
note: Name long predates 1793; from_year = map start. Label point estimated (open lake south of the Islands).

name: Don River
note: Name given by Lieutenant Governor Simcoe (source gives no year; Simcoe founded York 1793). Lower river straightened in the 1880s. Label point estimated.

name: Ashbridge's Bay
note: Five-square-kilometre marsh east of the harbour, named for Sarah Ashbridge. Toronto Harbour Commission began draining and filling it in 1912; by 1922, 200 ha filled, the rest later in the 1920s. Today the name survives only for a small bay and park near Coxwell (43.6593,-79.3109). from_year = map start; label point estimated for the former marsh.

name: Port Lands
note: Created by the Ashbridge's Bay Reclamation Scheme (started 1912); 200 ha filled by 1922, another 200 ha later in the 1920s. Source does not date the name 'Port Lands' itself.

name: Garrison Creek
note: Diverted into sewers starting in the 1870s; entirely in the sewer system by 1920. Label point = Trinity Bellwoods Park, which lies over the creek (park coordinates from the Trinity-Bellwoods article).

name: Taddle Creek
note: Buried in phases: east of Church St before 1860; Elizabeth St to Church St 1866; University of Toronto sections (McCaul's Pond) 1886. Label point estimated (Philosopher's Walk).

name: Old Town
note: Original ten-block townsite; name in use 'no later than 1815'. Label point estimated.

name: New Town
note: Jarvis St to Peter St, south of Queen and north of Front; sparsely populated in 1815, grew in the 1820s-1830s. No end date in the source: to_year 1834 (incorporation, when wards were created) is an editorial cut-off. Label point estimated.

name: Macaulaytown
note: Working-class subdivision of the Macaulay park lot, north of Lot (Queen) St and west of Yonge. No start year in any source opened (Macaulay granted the lot 1797; described as a shanty town around the time of incorporation). Absorbed into the city by 1834 as part of St. Patrick's Ward. Label point estimated.

name: The Ward
note: St. John's Ward split off from St. Patrick's Ward by 1852; known as the Ward. No end date in the source: to_year 1960 is an estimate based on the expropriation and demolition for the new City Hall starting in the late 1950s.

name: Cabbagetown
note: Name from Irish immigrants who arrived from the late 1840s; area first known as the village of Don Vale. No exact year for the name: 1850 used.

name: Corktown
note: Name 'originated in the early 19th century' (Irish immigrants said to be from County Cork). No year given, so from_year is blank. Label point estimated.

name: Yorkville
note: Founded 1830 by Joseph Bloor and William Botsford Jarvis; incorporated as a village 1853; annexed 1 February 1883.

name: Parkdale
note: Founded as an independent settlement 'in the 1850s' (decade only; 1850 used). Incorporated as a village 1879; annexed March 1889.

name: Brockton
note: Settlement grew along Brock Avenue (road built 1850) and took the name Brockton; unincorporated village 1876, incorporated 1880 (town 1881), annexed 1884.

name: Seaton Village
note: Laid out on the Crookshank farm 'in the 1850s' (decade only; 1850 used); annexed 1888. Never incorporated per sources opened. Coordinates from Wikipedia; annexation year also in https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Toronto

name: The Annex
note: Subdivision named 'the Toronto Annex' by developer Simeon Janes in 1886; annexed 1887.

name: Riverside
note: Area 'then called Riverside' (with Don Mount and Leslieville) annexed 1884: Don valley to Greenwood, Queen to Danforth. Earlier use of the name not dated in the source. Label point estimated (Queen and Broadview).

name: Leslieville
note: Began as a small village 'in the 1850s' around George Leslie's Toronto Nurseries (decade only; 1850 used); annexed 1884 with Riverside.

name: Rosedale
note: Jarvis estate settled 1826 and named Rosedale by Mary Jarvis (no year for the naming); estate subdivided 1854; annexed 1905.

name: The Junction
note: Village of West Toronto Junction founded 1884; Town of West Toronto Junction 1889; Town of Toronto Junction 1892; Town (source also says City) of West Toronto 1908; annexed 1909.

name: East Toronto
note: Area occupied from about 1850; incorporated as a village 1888, town 1903; annexed 1908.

name: North Toronto
note: Town of North Toronto incorporated 1890 (Bedford Park, Eglinton, Davisville); annexed 1912.

name: Deer Park
note: Named 1837 by the Heath family (40 acres at Yonge and St. Clair); subdivided 1846; annexed 1908.

name: Kensington Market
note: Denison estate (bought 1815) subdivided in the 1850s; became known as 'the Jewish Market' in the 1920s (decade only; 1920 used). Source does not date the name 'Kensington Market'.

name: Chinatown
note: First Chinatown, York and Elizabeth streets between Queen and Dundas: 'took shape in the early 1900s' (1900 used); lead says it existed 1890s-1970s. Two thirds expropriated and razed from the late 1950s for City Hall: to_year 1960 is an estimate. Label point estimated.

name: Chinatown
note: Spadina and Dundas. Businesses moved west 'during the 1950s and 1960s' after the first Chinatown was expropriated (no exact year; 1960 used).

name: Railway Lands
note: First railway (Ontario, Simcoe and Huron) arrived 1853; land south of Front filled for railways 1850s-1920s. Now largely CityPlace and South Core.

name: CityPlace
note: Land bought by Concord Adex 1997; first towers (Block 1) completed 2002.

name: Regent Park
note: Regent Park North approved 1947; first families moved in 1949 (source does not give 1948).

name: St. James Town
note: Area rezoned in the 1950s; first tower completed 1959, others 1965 and 1967. The source does not date the name itself.

name: Liberty Village
note: Named for Liberty Street. Source does not date the name; the earliest dated use is the Liberty Village BIA, founded 2001.

name: Distillery District
note: Gooderham and Worts distillery founded 1832, closed 1990; reopened to the public as the Distillery District on 22 May 2003. Label point estimated.

name: Harbourfront
note: Harbourfront project announced 1972 (York St to Bathurst St, south of Queens Quay); Harbourfront Corporation established 1972.

name: King's College
note: Royal charter 15 March 1827; renamed University of Toronto (legislation 1849, name assumed 1850). Label point = University of Toronto coordinates.

name: University of Toronto
note: King's College secularised and renamed; assumed present name in 1850.

name: Queen's Park
note: Opened and named 11 September 1860 by the Prince of Wales; land leased to the City 1859. Legislative Building completed 1892.

name: High Park
note: Howard conveyed the land 1873; opened to the public 1876.

name: Exhibition grounds
note: City leased the western garrison reserve April 1878; first Toronto Industrial Exhibition held 1879.

name: Trinity College
note: Opened January 1852 on Queen Street West; moved to Hoskin Avenue in 1925. Label point estimated: the south half of today's Trinity Bellwoods Park.

name: Hanlan's Point Amusement Park
note: Ferry company park opened 1897 (Hanlan's Point Beach article); burned 10 August 1909, rebuilt for 1910; demolished 1937 for the airport. Label point estimated: the north end of Hanlan's Point, now under the airport.
